headline: High-risk filesystem and git overlap in Claude Code can corrupt shared work; LightZero adds no direct mitigation or isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code ingests repo files and user-provided directories, and can use MCP; LightZero has no I/O surfaces or ingestion path. The pair therefore has a plausible prompt-injection bridge only if the user places attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs, not by default.
conditions: IF attacker-controlled text is written into a repo file or MCP-fed artifact that Claude Code reads
IF LightZero is later used to consume Claude Code's generated text as instructions
mitigations: Restrict Claude Code to trusted directories only
Disable MCP servers unless explicitly needed
Review generated files before passing them to LightZero
Use a separate workspace for untrusted inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, while LightZero exposes no filesystem or network surfaces. Leakage is plausible through shared workspace or git artifacts if Claude Code writes sensitive context into files that LightZero can later read indirectly via the same repo.
conditions: IF Claude Code writes secrets or sensitive code into shared repo files
IF LightZero is given access to the same workspace through an external wrapper or pipeline
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared repo
Use a throwaway working tree for Claude Code
Rotate any credentials exposed in shell environment
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive tasks into different directories
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. LightZero cannot write, so direct two-way conflict is limited; however, the dangerous default is Claude Code mutating shared git state without locking, which can corrupt work if another process depends on the same repo.
conditions: IF Claude Code and another process edit the same repo concurrently
IF git operations occur without external locking
mitigations: Pause other writers before running Claude Code
Commit or stash before handoff
Use per-agent branches
Run in a cloned repository
requires-engineering: add file/git locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can produce code or shell actions that LightZero may later treat as authoritative if the operator pipelines outputs between them. LightZero has no built-in verification or action authority in the profile, so the cascade is plausible but not inherently automatic.
conditions: IF Claude Code output is copied into LightZero-driven automation or evaluation
IF the operator skips manual verification between agents
mitigations: Require human review of Claude Code outputs
Insert a validation step before LightZero consumes results
Use structured output formats with checksums
Keep LightZero read-only with respect to Claude Code artifacts
requires-engineering: build an explicit verifier

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and shell environment secrets, while LightZero lists no data classes or residency/compliance commitments. The pair shows a limited compliance gap only if sensitive credentials are placed into Claude Code's environment; LightZero is not cited because it has no documented compliance surface here.
conditions: IF regulated data or credentials are present in Claude Code's shell environment
IF those secrets are written into shared files or logs
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shell environment
Use short-lived credentials
Avoid placing regulated data in the shared repo
Review logs before retention
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
